description: OpenRails for Simulation is a fork of the open-source Open Rails train simulator that lets a Python client drive the simulation over HTTP, so that Open Rails can serve as a railway simulation environment for systems engineering and testing. Commands sent to the Open Rails server control an ego train treated as the system under test, and the repository ships Python demo scripts, documentation and a co-simulation release that couples the simulator to other tools through an extension of the OpenMCx co-simulation framework. Tracks, routes and train models come from the free Open Rails content library. It is maintained by the German Aerospace Center under its DLR-SE organisation and is aimed at researchers, teachers and students of systems engineering and railway enthusiasts; the co-simulation release was archived on Zenodo on 27 February 2026. It is location independent and works at the scale of a single train on a route. The code is free on GitHub under GPL-3.0, with Windows builds of Open Rails and Python requirements. Caveats: users must build the Open Rails solution themselves, content must be obtained separately, and the simulation is driven from a game engine, not a validated train dynamics model. It supports digital twin and agent-based testing of train control functions and co-simulation of railway operations, and relates to OSRD, catalogued here.
